campaigns.subject: Is feeling anxious a sin?
campaigns.html:
Somebody told you that anxiety is a sin.

 

Maybe they said it straight out.

 

Maybe it was just a raised eyebrow when you admitted you were struggling.

 

Now you are carrying two things instead of one.

 

The anxious thought, and the guilt for having it.

 

That is a heavy way to live.

 

You stop praying about it because you are too ashamed to bring it up.

 

And false guilt pushes you away from God at the exact moment you need Him most.

 

But look at what happened the night before the cross.

 

Jesus went to a garden called Gethsemane to pray.

 

"My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death."

 

Luke says His sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.

 

And Hebrews says He was in all points tempted like as we are, "yet without sin."

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

Anxiety is a feeling, not a verdict.

 

If dread itself were sin, Jesus could not have felt it in Gethsemane and stayed sinless. But He did both.

 

That does not mean there is no line. The line is not the feeling. The line is what the feeling talks you into doing.

 

⚠️ When it hardens into a refusal to trust God

 

⚠️ When it drives you to control or manipulate people to feel safe

 

⚠️ When it becomes a reason to stop praying instead of a reason to pray more

 

God is not asking you to feel nothing. He is asking you to bring what you feel to Him.

 

Every anxious thought is raw material for prayer, not evidence against you.

 

In the full guide I walk through the difference between temptation and sin, what to do with false guilt, and eight ways to handle anxiety without the shame.

 

You can read it here:

 

Is Anxiety a Sin? What the Bible Actually Teaches

campaigns.subject: Nobody drifts from God all at once
campaigns.html:
Her name is still an insult three thousand years later.

 

Call somebody a Jezebel and everyone knows it is not a compliment.

 

But most people could not tell you what she actually did.

 

So here is what she did.

 

She was a Phoenician princess who married Ahab, king of Israel.

 

She brought Baal worship with her and made it national policy.

 

She fed the prophets of Baal at her own table while she hunted the prophets of the LORD.

 

And when Ahab wanted a vineyard that was not his, she called a fast, paid two men to lie, and had an innocent man named Naboth stoned to death.

 

She never had to force a nation to walk away from God.

 

Nobody announced they were abandoning Him.

 

They just started adding Baal alongside the LORD.

 

Until Elijah stood up and asked, "How long halt ye between two opinions?"

 

And the people answered him not a word.

 

That is the kind of influence I want you to watch for.

 

The most dangerous influence does not force you away from God. It makes drifting feel normal.

 

It usually comes through someone close to you.

 

It comes wrapped in something that looks harmless.

 

And it happens slowly, one small compromise at a time.

 

Jesus even brought her name up again in Revelation, rebuking a church for tolerating "that woman Jezebel."

 

So her story leaves you with two honest questions.

 

❓ Who is influencing you, and toward what?

campaigns.subject: Can you name all six pieces?
campaigns.html:
You know the phrase "the armor of God."

 

You have probably seen the picture. A soldier, each piece labeled with a Bible word.

 

Maybe you even prayed it once during a hard week.

 

But if someone asked you right now, could you name all six pieces?

 

Paul did not write this from a place of comfort.

 

He wrote Ephesians from a Roman prison, chained to a guard.

 

And he was not writing about spooky battles.

 

He was writing to ordinary Christians about staying on their feet when life pushes back.

 

Here is each piece, in the order Paul gives them.

 

🛡️ Belt of truth: holds everything else in place

 

🛡️ Breastplate of righteousness: Christ's righteousness, not your own

 

🛡️ Shoes of the gospel of peace: footing that holds on rough ground

 

🛡️ Shield of faith: stops the fiery darts before they land

 

🛡️ Helmet of salvation: guards your mind against despair

 

Every one of those is defense. Then comes the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, the only offensive piece in the whole passage.

 

A vague feeling cannot cut through a specific lie. A specific verse can.

 

But most graphics stop there. Paul does not.

 

The very next verse says, "Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit."

 

Prayer is not a seventh piece of armor. It is how the other six actually get worn.

 

The armor was never about winning one dramatic battle. It is about still standing.

 

Paul repeats the word stand three times in this passage.

 

And he reminds you who the fight is really against. "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood."

 

In the full guide I walk through Ephesians 6:10 to 18 piece by piece, what each part of a Roman soldier's armor actually did, and seven practical ways to put it on today.

 

You can read it here:

campaigns.subject: What is quietly pulling you from God?
campaigns.html:
You want to be closer to God.

 

You want to pray more and read your Bible more.

 

You want to feel less guilty when Sunday rolls around.

 

But something keeps getting in the way.

 

Most men do not wake up one day and decide to walk away from God.

 

It happens slowly.

 

One skipped prayer becomes a pattern.

 

One private compromise becomes a hidden life.

 

So I wrote about five of the biggest things quietly pulling men away from God.

 

🔥 Lust: it promises satisfaction and leaves you emptier

 

😴 Passive faith: believing in God without pursuing Him

 

💼 Worldly goals: anything in first place besides God becomes an idol

 

📱 Toxic entertainment: everything you consume is discipling you

 

🤝 Weak friendships: the men around you shape the man you are becoming

 

None of these show up with a warning label.

 

But none of them have to define your life either.

 

Joseph did not negotiate with temptation. He left his coat behind and ran.

 

Moses grew up with every advantage in Pharaoh's palace, and he walked away from all of it.

 

The world can sharpen your habits, but only God can change your heart.

 

Discipline without Jesus just produces a cleaner version of the same empty life.

 

God is not looking for perfect men. He is looking for surrendered ones.

 

Be honest about which of the five you struggle with most. That is often exactly where God wants to begin.

 

In the full guide I walk through what Scripture says about each one, the men in the Bible who faced the same fight, and seven things you can start doing today.

 

You can read it here:

 

5 Things Holding Men Back From God (And How to Break Free)

campaigns.subject: Where did the pitchfork come from?
campaigns.html:
Maybe you grew up scared of a cartoon devil with a pitchfork.

 

Red suit. Horns. Flames everywhere.

 

And somewhere along the way, you stopped being sure how much of that is actually in the Bible.

 

Here is the honest answer. Most of it came from movies and medieval paintings.

 

Not from Scripture.

 

The real picture in the Bible is more careful than that.

 

It unfolds in stages instead of arriving all at once.

 

Our English Bibles often flatten several different ideas into one word, hell.

 

📜 Sheol, the Old Testament word for the realm of the dead

 

📜 Hades, the Greek word the New Testament uses the same way

 

📜 Gehenna, the word Jesus used for final judgment

 

🔥 The lake of fire, hell's final and permanent form

 

Each one means something a little different, and the differences actually matter.

 

But there is one line in Matthew 25 I do not want you to miss.

 

"Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels."

 

Prepared for the devil and his angels.

 

Not originally for people.

 

Hell was never God's desired ending for you. The cross is His answer to it.

 

Jesus talked about hell more than almost anyone else in Scripture.

 

Not to scare people for no reason. He talked about it because He loves people, and eternity is real.

 

That is why this is worth understanding, not avoiding.

 

In the full guide I walk through each word, what happens after death, where faithful Christians disagree about whether hell lasts forever, and how to comfort someone who is grieving.

 

It is heavy ground, so take it slow.

 

You can read it here:

 

What Is Hell? What the Bible Actually Says

 

It is completely free, just like everything else inside Bible Buddy.

campaigns.subject: Why is there light before the sun?
campaigns.html:
You have probably heard Genesis 1 argued about more than you have heard it read.

 

Six days or millions of years.

 

Science or faith.

 

Somebody online is always sure.

 

But have you ever sat down and read the whole chapter, start to finish?

 

It only takes a few minutes.

 

And when you do, you start noticing things.

 

Light shows up on day one. The sun does not show up until day four.

 

That is not a mistake. The text is deliberate about it.

 

Then there is the pattern hiding in plain sight.

 

Days one through three form the spaces. Light and dark, sky and sea, land and plants.

 

Days four through six fill those same spaces, in the same order.

 

God builds the rooms before He moves anything into them.

 

And on day six, He does something He has not done for anything else He made.

 

"So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them."

 

No star. No animal. Only the man and the woman, both equally.

 

You are not an accident. You were made in God's image, on purpose.

 

And before anyone had done a single thing, God looked at it all and called it very good.

 

Your worth started there. Not with anything you accomplish.

 

So I put together a plain English walkthrough of Genesis 1.

 

📅 What happens on each of the six days, in order

 

🌅 Why light shows up before the sun

 

👤 What it means to be made in God's image

 

📖 Why John 1 opens with the same words as Genesis 1

 

It is a chapter overview, so you can see the whole shape of the week before you study it one verse at a time.

 

You can read it here:

 

Genesis 1 Explained: The Creation of the World

campaigns.subject: She was probably a teenager
campaigns.html:
She was probably a teenager.

 

No army. No title. No wealth.

 

Just a poor girl from a small town called Nazareth.

 

And an angel showed up and asked her to carry the Son of God.

 

We hear Mary's name every Christmas. But think about what her yes actually meant.

 

An unmarried, pregnant girl in a small town where everyone would count the months.

 

A fiance who could have walked away and been fully within his rights.

 

Whispers she would carry for the rest of her life.

 

She said yes anyway.

 

"Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word."

 

She said that before she had a single answer to how it would work or what it would cost her.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

God did not need status or wealth for His biggest plan. He needed a willing heart.

 

Mary did not understand everything about her son.

 

When the shepherds came, Scripture says she "kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart."

 

At the temple, an old man named Simeon told her a sword would pierce through her own soul.

 

Years later, at a wedding in Cana, she pointed the servants to her son: "Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it."

 

And when she finally stood near the cross, she watched Simeon's word come true.

 

But the last picture Scripture gives us of Mary is not grief. It is a woman still praying with the believers.

 

This Christmas, when you hear her name, I hope you see the courage behind it.

 

In the full article I walk through her whole story in order, from Gabriel's visit to the wedding at Cana to the upper room in Acts.

 

You can read it here:

 

Who Was Mary, the Mother of Jesus? The Woman God Chose to Carry His Son

 

It is completely free, just like everything else inside Bible Buddy.

campaigns.subject: Anxiety does not knock first
campaigns.html:
Anxiety does not knock first.

 

It shows up in the middle of the night.

 

It shows up when the bank account is low and the Christmas list is not.

 

It follows you into the family dinner and sits in your chest the whole time.

 

And sometimes another Christian tells you to just have more faith.

 

That one stings the most.

 

Because it makes your anxiety feel like proof that something is wrong with your walk with God.

 

Here is what I want you to hear. You are not a bad Christian.

 

David lay awake at night, soaking his bed with tears.

 

Martha was so anxious about serving dinner that she missed Jesus sitting in her living room.

 

Jesus did not scold her for the dinner. He named what was happening inside her.

 

"Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things."

 

God does not give anxiety a rebuke. He gives it a replacement.

 

"Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."

 

In the old King James language, "be careful for nothing" means be anxious about nothing.

 

Then comes the promise. The peace of God "shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."

 

That word keep means to guard, like a soldier standing watch at the gate.

 

Faith is not the absence of anxiety. Faith is where you carry it.

 

So this week, when the spiral starts, say the worry to God out loud, by name.

 

And if anxiety is crushing you day after day, seeing a doctor or counselor is not weak faith. God works through wise helpers too.

 

In the full guide I walk through what Jesus taught about worry, five verses to hold onto, and honest answers to questions like whether anxiety is a sin.

 

You can read it here:

It shows up in the middle of the night.

 

It shows up when the bank account is low and the Christmas list is not.

 

It follows you into the family dinner and sits in your chest the whole time.

 

And sometimes another Christian tells you to just have more faith.

 

That one stings the most.

 

Because it makes your anxiety feel like proof that something is wrong with your walk with God.

 

Here is what I want you to hear. You are not a bad Christian.

 

David lay awake at night, soaking his bed with tears.

 

Martha was so anxious about serving dinner that she missed Jesus sitting in her living room.

 

Jesus did not scold her for the dinner. He named what was happening inside her.

 

"Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things."

 

God does not give anxiety a rebuke. He gives it a replacement.

 

"Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."

 

In the old King James language, "be careful for nothing" means be anxious about nothing.

 

Then comes the promise. The peace of God "shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."

 

That word keep means to guard, like a soldier standing watch at the gate.

 

Faith is not the absence of anxiety. Faith is where you carry it.

 

So this week, when the spiral starts, say the worry to God out loud, by name.

 

And if anxiety is crushing you day after day, seeing a doctor or counselor is not weak faith. God works through wise helpers too.

 

In the full guide I walk through what Jesus taught about worry, five verses to hold onto, and honest answers to questions like whether anxiety is a sin.

 

You can read it here:

campaigns.subject: Different churches, one table
campaigns.html:
This week, a lot of families will sit down around one table.

 

And not everyone at that table goes to the same church.

 

Maybe one side of the family is Baptist, and the other side is Catholic.

 

Maybe a cousin just found a non denominational church and cannot stop talking about it.

 

And somewhere between the turkey and the pie, the question comes up.

 

If we all read the same Bible, why are there so many denominations?

 

Maybe you have even been told yours is the only one that really gets it right.

 

Here is what might surprise you.

 

Jesus never started a denomination. The apostles never founded one either.

 

What you see today is nearly two thousand years of history, culture, courage, and human weakness, all tangled together.

 

⛪ The Great Schism of 1054, mostly a fight about authority

 

📖 The Reformation, a call back to Scripture

 

👥 And yes, some splits that were just pride and personality clashing

 

But most denominations still hold the same essentials.

 

Jesus is Lord. He died for sin and rose again. Salvation is by grace through faith.

 

Unity in Christ was never about agreeing on every detail. It rests on a shared faith in who Jesus is and what He did.

 

Jesus prayed for that unity the night before He went to the cross.

 

"That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me."

 

So here is one thing to carry to your table this Thanksgiving.

 

Look for what you share before you look for what divides you.

 

You will probably find more in common than you expected.

 

In the full guide I walk through the real history, what is actually at stake when Christians divide, and how to choose a church home without picking a fight.

 

You can read it here:

 

Why So Many Denominations?

 

It is completely free, just like everything else inside Bible Buddy.

I am so glad you are here, and I did not want Christmas to pass without saying that to you.

campaigns.subject: KJV, NIV, ESV, NLT. Which one?
campaigns.html:
You go to buy someone a Bible for Christmas.

 

And there is not one Bible to choose from.

 

There is a whole list.

 

KJV. NIV. ESV. NLT. NASB. NKJV. CSB.

 

So which one is the real Bible?

 

Maybe someone told you only one version counts.

 

Maybe you grabbed whatever your church uses and never asked why.

 

Or maybe you quietly wondered if the Bible has been changed over the years.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

The Bible was never written in English. Every English Bible is a translation of the same message.

 

The Old Testament was written mostly in Hebrew, with a few parts in Aramaic. The New Testament was written in Greek.

 

That is not a weakness. It is what lets God's Word reach every generation in its own language.

 

Almost every difference you notice between versions comes down to one of three approaches.

 

📝 Word for word: KJV, NKJV, NASB, ESV

 

📖 Thought for thought: NIV, CSB, NLT

 

💬 Paraphrase: The Message

 

Different words. Same truth.

 

Put John 3:16 side by side in four translations and the meaning does not move an inch. Only the phrasing does.

 

So if you are picking a Bible for someone this season, the better question is not which one is right. It is which one fits the person.

 

An NIV or NLT for a new believer. A KJV or NKJV for someone who loves to memorize and read aloud. An ESV or NASB for deep study.

 

In the full guide I walk through the real history of seven major translations and show John 3:16, Psalm 23:1 and Philippians 4:13 side by side.

 

You can read it here:

 

Why Are There So Many Bible Translations? A Complete Guide

campaigns.subject: Read the whole Bible in 2027?
campaigns.html:
Every January, a lot of us make the same promise.

 

This is the year I read the whole Bible.

 

And a few weeks later, the bookmark is stuck somewhere in the middle.

 

Most people think reading the Bible and studying the Bible are the same thing.

 

They are not.

 

You open a passage. Read a chapter. Close the book. Move on.

 

Finishing chapters feels like progress. But it does not always change much.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

The goal is not to check a box. The goal is to understand what God is saying.

Joseph. Moses. David. Israel. Jesus. Paul. Each story stands on its own, and each one connects.

 

When you read it that way, the stories stick and the whole Bible starts to make sense.

 

Slow down. Ask questions. Seek context. Follow the story.

campaigns.subject: What would you say if they asked?
campaigns.html:
Someone asks you, "Why do you believe in Jesus?"

 

And for a second, your mind goes blank.

 

You believe every word of your answer.

 

You just cannot find it fast enough.

 

So you say, "I just have faith."

 

That is not wrong. But it does not go deep enough.

 

Coworkers ask. Kids ask.

 

Your own doubts ask, usually at the worst possible hour of the night.

 

And unanswered questions do not stay quiet. They grow.

 

Here is the good news.

 

You do not need a hundred arguments memorized. You need one, understood well.

 

Faith is not blind. It is built on something that actually happened.

 

"And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain."

 

Paul staked everything on the resurrection. And the evidence for it is stronger than most Christians realize.

 

👥 Over 500 people saw Jesus alive at once

 

👣 The first witnesses were women, a detail no one inventing the story would choose

 

🔥 Frightened men who ran on Friday were preaching boldly by Sunday

 

People do not willingly die for something they know they made up.

 

But the Bible also cares about how you give your answer.

 

Peter says to be ready always to give an answer, "with meekness and fear."

 

The goal was never to win the argument. The goal is to point to Jesus.

 

In the full guide I walk through the evidence step by step, plus eight simple ways to start getting ready this week.

 

You can read it here:

 

How to Defend Your Faith in Jesus

campaigns.subject: What if one more sin is too many?
campaigns.html:
You did the thing again.

 

The sin you promised God you were done with.

 

And now a voice in your head will not stop asking one question.

 

Can one more failure be the thing that finally undoes it?

 

If that question has kept you up at night, you are not alone.

 

It is one of the most asked questions in the whole Christian life.

 

And the Bible does not dodge it.

 

Jesus said of His sheep, "they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

 

Then He adds the Father's hand too. Two hands, not one.

 

But I also want to be honest with you.

 

Hebrews and 2 Peter carry real warnings about falling away.

 

Good, sincere, Bible believing Christians read those passages and land in different places.

 

Neither side is reading Scripture carelessly.

 

Here is where both sides actually meet.

 

Your assurance was never meant to rest on your performance. It rests on Christ.

 

John wrote a whole letter so you could know, not guess, that you have eternal life.

 

And he gave you the way back when you fail.

 

"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

 

Faithful and just. Not moody. Not keeping score.

 

And a heart still afraid of losing Him is usually a heart He still holds.

 

In the full guide I walk through the promises, the warnings, the two ways faithful Christians read them, and eight ways to walk in assurance instead of fear.

 

Take a breath before you start.

 

You can read it here:

 

Can You Lose Your Salvation? What the Bible Says

campaigns.subject: Only two men got this description
campaigns.html:
You have probably seen the list on a pin somewhere.

 

Men who walked with God in the Bible.

 

It looks simple.

 

It is not as simple as most graphics make it look.

 

Scripture only uses the exact words "walked with God" about two men.

 

Enoch and Noah.

 

Abraham is called the Friend of God. Moses spoke with the LORD face to face.

 

Close, faithful lives. Just described in different words.

 

And the two men who did get that description teach you something important.

 

Enoch walked with God for three hundred years.

 

Not three hundred good days. Three hundred years.

 

Noah kept walking with God while nearly everyone around him had stopped.

 

God warned him about a flood no one had ever seen, and Noah built a boat on dry land.

 

Faithfulness will sometimes look out of step with everyone around you.

 

Walking with God is not one dramatic moment. It is one ordinary day connected to the next.

 

A walk is steady. It has a direction, and God sets it.

 

And that walk is not reserved for two men in Genesis.

 

"He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?"

 

Micah puts that same walk in front of every reader. Including you.

 

In the full guide I walk through Enoch, Noah, the other faithful men Scripture describes in different words, and what this looks like for you today.

 

It is a short read, and a good one to sit with.

 

You can read it here:

 

Every Man Who Walked With God in the Bible

campaigns.subject: Why Paul said fruit, not fruits
campaigns.html:
You can probably recite the list from memory.

 

Love. Joy. Peace. Patience. Kindness. Goodness. Faithfulness. Gentleness. Self control.

 

Maybe you learned it as a kid, one word per finger.

 

And then you lose your temper in traffic five minutes later.

 

Or you pray for more patience and lose it anyway by lunch.

 

Or you read Galatians 5 and feel guilty on eight out of nine.

 

If that is you, you are not failing at Christianity.

 

You are human, and fruit takes time.

 

Here is a small detail that changes everything.

 

Paul did not write fruits. He wrote fruit. Singular.

 

"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."

 

One fruit with nine parts. It grows together, or it does not grow at all.

 

The fruit of the Spirit is not a checklist you climb. It is what grows in you when you stay close to Jesus.

 

A branch does not grunt out apples by trying harder.

 

It stays attached to the vine, and the vine does the rest.

 

"I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing."

 

That does not make growth easy. It means the source is different.

 

Longsuffering only grows around people who are hard to love.

 

Temperance stands guard over all the others.

 

And slow growth is still growth.

 

He is not in a hurry with you.

 

In the full guide I walk through all nine, one at a time, straight from Galatians 5, with six simple ways to stay planted where the fruit can grow.

 

You can read it here:

 

What Is the Fruit of the Spirit? All 9 Explained

campaigns.html:
Most of us have held a Bible without ever asking what it actually is.

 

It sits on a shelf. Or in an app on your phone.

 

It looks like one book.

 

But the Bible is not just a book. It is a library.

 

📚 Sixty six books

 

✍️ Written by over forty authors

 

🌍 In three languages, across three continents

 

🕰️ Over roughly 1,500 years

 

Empires rose and fell while it was being written. Languages shifted. Cultures changed.

 

Think about who wrote it.

 

A king. A shepherd. A fisherman. A tax collector. A physician. A man who used to persecute Christians.

 

Different backgrounds. Different personalities.

 

And yet the central message never changed.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

The Bible is one story. Not about people reaching up to God, but about God reaching down to us.

 

Genesis plants the seed. Micah names Bethlehem. Psalm 22 paints the crucifixion before crucifixion existed.

 

A tree in Genesis. A cross in the Gospels. A tree of life again in Revelation.

 

That is not random. That is design.

 

And once you understand how the Bible is put together, a lot of the confusion starts to fade.

campaigns.subject: When someone you trusted turns on you
campaigns.html:
Somebody you trusted turned on you.

 

A door you did not deserve got slammed shut anyway.

 

And now you are sitting in a season that makes no sense, wondering if God even sees it.

 

That is exactly where Joseph's story starts.

 

A favorite son, thrown in a pit by his own brothers.

 

Sold for twenty pieces of silver.

 

Falsely accused. Thrown in prison. Forgotten by the one man who could have spoken up for him.

 

Thirteen years passed between the pit and the palace.

 

But Scripture keeps repeating one line, on purpose.

 

"And the LORD was with Joseph."

 

In a slave owner's house. In a prison cell. Before anything got better.

 

God's presence was never a reward for Joseph's circumstances improving. It was the constant underneath every one of them.

 

And the ending is not the one you would expect.

 

Judah, the brother who suggested selling Joseph, later offers himself as a slave to save his youngest brother.

 

Then Joseph looks his betrayers in the face and chooses forgiveness instead of revenge.

 

Listen to what he tells them.

 

"But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive."

 

He does not pretend the evil never happened.

 

He holds both things at once. What you did was evil. And God used it for good.

 

You may not be in a pit or a prison. But the season you are in is not empty either.

 

In the full guide I walk through the whole story in order, from the dreams to the palace, with five lessons from Joseph's life.

campaigns.subject: What heaven is really like
campaigns.html:
The holidays have a way of making an empty chair feel louder.

 

The decorations come out. The songs start playing.

 

And somewhere in the middle of it, you miss someone.

 

If that is you this year, I am sorry. I wanted to write to you gently today.

 

When we miss someone who loved Jesus, we start to wonder about heaven.

 

Most of us picture clouds. White robes. Harps. Floating.

 

Something vague and bright and far away.

 

But the Bible describes something far better than a cartoon in the sky.

 

When a believer dies, Scripture says they go to be with Christ.

 

Paul put it this way: "absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord."

 

🕊️ Conscious

 

🕊️ With the Lord

 

🕊️ In peace

 

And that is not even the end of the story.

 

The Bible does not end with us going up. It ends with heaven coming down.

 

A new heaven and a new earth, where God dwells with His people.

 

No more death. No more mourning. No more crying. No more pain.

 

Heaven is not clouds. It is closeness. God fully present with His people, and death defeated.

 

Revelation 22:4 says it simply: "they shall see his face."

 

If you are carrying grief this season, I hope that gives you something steady to hold onto.

 

In the full article I walk through what heaven is right now, what happens when a believer dies, and the new creation Revelation promises.

 

You can read it here:

campaigns.subject: What about the ones who never heard?
campaigns.html:
Maybe it is your grandfather.

 

Someone who lived his whole life where nobody ever said the name of Jesus to him.

 

Or a friend who died before you found the courage to say anything.

 

Whoever it is for you, this question has a face.

 

What happens to people who never heard of Jesus?

 

It is one of the heaviest questions a Christian can carry.

 

Because underneath it is a quieter fear.

 

Was God fair to someone I loved?

 

I want to be honest with you.

 

Scripture does not hand us a complete formula for this exact question.

 

Anyone who tells you they know for sure, in either direction, is saying more than the Bible actually says.

 

But the Bible does give us something real.

 

🌅 Creation is a witness. Romans 1 says God "hath shewed it unto them."

 

❤️ Conscience is a witness. Romans 2 says the work of the law is "written in their hearts."

 

⚖️ And God's character is the anchor we can stand on.

 

Abraham once brought God almost this exact question.

 

God was about to judge Sodom, and Abraham asked, "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?"

 

He did not get every detail. He got confidence in the One doing the judging.

 

You do not get every detail of the verdict. You do get the character of the Judge.

 

And none of this makes the gospel less urgent. Romans 10:14 asks how anyone will hear without a preacher.

 

The ache you feel about someone in the past is a strong reason to speak up to someone in your life now.

 

In the full article I walk through Romans 1 and 2, Genesis 18, and the verses that help you hold this question with open hands.

campaigns.subject: She waited a lifetime for this
campaigns.html:
Some Bible stories start with a battle. Elizabeth's starts with a wait.

 

She was married to a good man. She loved God with her whole life.

 

And year after year, the one thing she wanted most never came.

 

In her world, a woman without children carried a quiet shame that never really let up.

 

But Luke goes out of his way to tell us she did nothing wrong.

 

"And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless."

 

Two faithful people. No child. Old age arriving with the door still shut.

 

Then one day an angel stood in the temple and spoke to her husband.

 

"Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

 

Thy prayer is heard.

 

Not a new prayer. An old one, prayed through all the years when nothing seemed to change.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

God's silence is not the same as God's absence.

 

Elizabeth hid herself for five months, then said the Lord had looked on her "to take away my reproach among men."

 

In her sixth month, her young relative Mary showed up at the door carrying a secret of her own.

 

The baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb, and she was filled with the Holy Ghost.

 

She called Mary "the mother of my Lord" and celebrated Mary's miracle right in the middle of her own.

 

Her long wait and the birth of Jesus ended up woven into the very same story.

 

She did not manufacture her miracle. She kept walking with God through years that gave her every reason to give up.

 

If you are waiting on something this Christmas that feels impossible, her story is for you.

 

In the full article I walk through Luke 1 in order, all the way to the day she stood against the whole family and said, "Not so; but he shall be called John."

campaigns.subject: Does 7 really mean something?
campaigns.html:
You have probably seen the chart.

 

Seven means completion. Forty means testing. Twelve means God's people.

 

A neat little graphic, saved from Pinterest, promising a secret code hidden just under the surface of the Bible.

 

Some of that chart is true.

 

Some of it is folk tradition dressed up as Bible fact.

 

And you deserve to know which is which before you build your faith on it.

 

Here is what I want you to understand.

 

A real pattern gets a real verse. A popular claim without one is just a guess.

 

God really does use numbers with intention.

 

✅ Seven: God rested on the seventh day and blessed it.

 

✅ Twelve: twelve tribes of Israel, then twelve apostles.

 

✅ Forty: the flood, the wilderness, and Jesus fasting before His ministry began.

 

✅ Three: Jesus pointed to Jonah's three days to explain His own resurrection.

 

Those patterns show up again and again, written by different people, hundreds of years apart.

 

That is not superstition. That is design.

 

But not every number has that kind of backing.

 

There is no verse that says five means grace.

 

And sixty six is simply how many books the Protestant Bible has. It is a fact about history, not a code.

 

Even 666 in Revelation 13:18 calls for wisdom, not confident guesses about who it points to today.

 

In the full guide I walk through one, three, six, seven, ten, twelve, forty, fifty and 666, each with the actual verse behind it.

 

Then you can let a real pattern teach you about God, and let a coincidence stay a coincidence.

 

You can read it here:

 

Biblical Numbers and Their Meanings: What Scripture Actually Teaches

campaigns.html:
Everything God made in Genesis 1 was good.

 

Light. Land. Sea. Stars. Animals.

 

And by the end of day six, very good.

 

Then Genesis 2 pulls the camera in close, and God says something surprising.

 

"It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him."

 

Not good.

 

It is the first negative statement in the entire Bible.

 

And it came before anything had gone wrong.

 

Adam had everything that should have satisfied him.

 

A garden. A job. One clear command. God's own presence.

 

And God still said something was missing.

 

Your need for other people is not a weakness. It was built into God's design from the very beginning.

 

God named that need before Adam even knew to feel it.

 

If you have ever felt ashamed of being lonely, you can stop carrying that shame.

 

Genesis 2 answers a lot of other questions Genesis 1 leaves open, too.

 

🏺 How God formed the first man from dust and His own breath

 

🌳 Why work was a gift in Eden, not a punishment

 

🦁 Why Adam named the animals before Eve was made

 

💍 What leave, cleave, and one flesh actually mean

 

Whatever season you are in, single, married, or just lonely tonight, this chapter has something to say to you.

 

In the full guide I walk through the chapter in order, so you see what the text actually says before you take anyone's word for it.

campaigns.subject: What if I am not really saved?
campaigns.html:
It is late. The house is quiet.

 

And a question shows up that you cannot pray away.

 

What if I am not really saved?

 

You believe in Jesus. But you still sin. You still doubt.

 

You still have days when God feels far away.

 

You are not the first person to lie awake with that question.

 

Christians who love God deeply have asked it for as long as the church has existed.

 

And John wrote a whole letter so people like you could stop guessing.

 

"That ye may know that ye have eternal life."

 

Here is the ground everything else stands on.

 

Salvation is not something you earn. It is something you receive by faith.

 

But real faith never leaves a person unchanged. It always leaves evidence behind.

 

So I walked through six signs from Scripture that your faith is real.

 

Not six things you do to earn it. Six things God does in someone He has actually saved. Here are three of them:

 

🟢 Sin bothers you now, when it used to just feel like living

 

🟢 You keep turning away from it, even after you have failed before

 

🟢 You genuinely want to know and obey God, not just survive Him

 

None of that means perfect. Struggling with sin is not the same thing as being ruled by it.

 

The question was never how perfect you are. It is which direction you are facing.

 

Look for the fruit, not perfection.

 

And if you care this much about the answer, that itself is worth paying attention to.

 

Not a courtroom. A conversation.

 

In the full guide I walk through all six signs, five verses on assurance, and honest answers to the questions people are afraid to ask, like what to do when you do not feel saved.

 

You can read it here:

And a question shows up that you cannot pray away.

 

What if I am not really saved?

 

You believe in Jesus. But you still sin. You still doubt.

 

You still have days when God feels far away.

 

You are not the first person to lie awake with that question.

 

Christians who love God deeply have asked it for as long as the church has existed.

 

And John wrote a whole letter so people like you could stop guessing.

 

"That ye may know that ye have eternal life."

 

Here is the ground everything else stands on.

 

Salvation is not something you earn. It is something you receive by faith.

 

But real faith never leaves a person unchanged. It always leaves evidence behind.

 

So I walked through six signs from Scripture that your faith is real.

 

Not six things you do to earn it. Six things God does in someone He has actually saved. Here are three of them:

 

🟢 Sin bothers you now, when it used to just feel like living

 

🟢 You keep turning away from it, even after you have failed before

 

🟢 You genuinely want to know and obey God, not just survive Him

 

None of that means perfect. Struggling with sin is not the same thing as being ruled by it.

 

The question was never how perfect you are. It is which direction you are facing.

 

Look for the fruit, not perfection.

 

And if you care this much about the answer, that itself is worth paying attention to.

 

Not a courtroom. A conversation.

 

In the full guide I walk through all six signs, five verses on assurance, and honest answers to the questions people are afraid to ask, like what to do when you do not feel saved.

 

You can read it here:

 

How Do You Know You Are Saved? 6 Biblical Signs Your Faith Is Real

campaigns.subject: Ever feel like the second choice?
campaigns.html:
You know that specific ache of being the one people settle for.

 

A room where nobody said your name.

 

A person who never picked you back.

 

A sister, a coworker, a friend who always seemed to be the favorite.

 

Leah lived her entire adult life inside that ache.

 

The Bible introduces her right next to her younger sister, and it is brutal.

 

"Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured."

 

Jacob loved Rachel and worked seven years to marry her.

 

Then on the wedding night, their father swapped the daughters.

 

"And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah."

 

Everyone in the story overlooked her. God did not.

 

"And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb."

 

She named her first three sons hoping her husband would finally love her.

 

It never worked.

 

Then came her fourth son, and she said something different. "Now will I praise the LORD." She named him Judah.

 

And here is the part that should give you chills.

 

From the tribe of Judah came King David. From the line of David came Jesus.

 

The Messiah did not come through the loved and chosen sister. He came through Leah.

 

She never knew any of it. She died thinking she was the wife nobody wanted.

 

So let me say this as plainly as I can.

 

Being unwanted by people is not the same as being unseen by God.

 

You can be invisible in a room and fully known by heaven at the same time.

 

In the full guide I walk through her whole story, the quiet detail about where Jacob chose to be buried, and six lessons from her life.

 

You can read it here:

 

Who Was Leah in the Bible? The Story of the Unloved Wife

 

It is completely free, just like everything else inside Bible Buddy.

campaigns.subject: Who gave the stars their names?
campaigns.html:
This is the weekend a lot of the world gets curious about the unseen.

 

Questions about spirits, fortunes, and the future come up more than usual.

 

But one of the most common ones never feels spooky at all.

 

It shows up on your phone before your coffee is done.

 

Your horoscope.

 

Most of us never thought of zodiac signs as a big deal.

 

It feels like a personality quiz wearing a prettier name.

 

A fun read. A tidy explanation for why you are the way you are.

 

Here is what most Christians have never been told.

 

Scripture names astrology directly, right alongside divination and witchcraft, and calls it an abomination unto the LORD.

 

That sounds harsh for something that feels this harmless.

 

But the reason has nothing to do with God wanting you to have less fun.

 

It has everything to do with where you go looking for answers about your life.

 

Astrology quietly hands three questions to the planets.

 

❓ Who made you who you are?

 

❓ Who actually knows what tomorrow holds?

 

❓ Who gets to define your identity and your future?

 

The stars were never in charge of you. God made every one of them, and He knows them all by name.

 

"He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names."

 

Even the star of Bethlehem did not tell the wise men anything about themselves.

 

It pointed straight at Jesus. And they worshipped Him, not the star.

 

In the full guide I walk through what Scripture says, answer honest questions like whether it is a sin to know your sign, and share seven simple ways to start asking God first.

 

Not to scare you. Not to shame you.

 

You can read it here:

 

What Does the Bible Say About Zodiac Signs?

 

It is completely free, just like everything else inside Bible Buddy.

 

Louis
